key: And all these blessings shall come upon thee, and overtake thee, if thou shalt hearken unto the voice of the LORD thy God.
s: Moses sets the blessings for hearkening before the curses that fill the chapter; Sforno, on 28:2, reads them as blessings that overtake Israel without striving, when Torah is its fixed pursuit and its labour only occasional.

reason: verse.js ok (exact), ref Deuteronomy 28:2 and at [180,2] match. Plain sense faithful: the blessings (28:1 to 14) conditional on hearkening stand before the curses of 28:15 to 68, which fill most of the chapter; no four-word run from the key. Opened every packet source on 28:2: Sforno comments twice, first that the blessings overtake you even though you do not strive to attain them (אע"פ שלא תשתדל אתה להשיגם), then on ‘if thou shalt hearken’ that this is when Torah is fixed and work occasional, so the blessings overtake without striving; he goes on to tie the blessings to the First Temple and the start of the Second, which the sentence does not use. Ibn Ezra says similarly that they come by themselves and you will not tire (no disagreement to name); Rashi, Ramban, Rashbam and Deuteronomy Rabbah have nothing on the verse. The paraphrase stays inside Sforno’s words. entry-check ok.
